the_signal.headline: Event delivery patterns separate reliable workflows from chaos
the_signal.body: The transactional outbox pattern is now table stakes for AI workflow reliability — it prevents dual writes and guarantees event delivery at scale. GTM engineers building revenue automation need this: one failed event sync means lost leads, broken handoffs, and revenue leakage. Without it, your workflow orchestration is just hopeful guessing.

tool_drop.name: ZenABN - Create LinkedIn Ads with AI
tool_drop.what: AI-powered LinkedIn ad generation tool that automates campaign creation.
tool_drop.why: Direct signal that ABM workflows are moving into pure AI generation — GTM teams should test whether this reduces ad ops friction or adds more validation overhead.

thread_of_day.title: API Rate Limiting for More Reliable Workflows
thread_of_day.takeaway: Rate limiting failures don't have to tank workflows — smart retry patterns, batching, and pacing turn 429s into a solved problem instead of a cascade failure.

quote.text: Choose a model, the tools and workflows it can use, and it's ready to go — n8n Agents now ship as a core orchestration primitive.

whats_moving.context: Deterministic vs. dynamic vs. agentic execution models are now explicitly differentiated — GTM teams need to know which one their revenue workflows actually are.
n8n Gateway Credits skip account setup and API key generation for model trials — the friction tax on trying new AI models is collapsing.
Visibility into workflow execution is now called out as core production challenge — teams blind to their orchestration are leaving money on the table.

act_on_this: Audit your top 3 revenue workflows for event delivery failure modes — map where dual writes could break sync and add transactional outbox pattern to the backlog this sprint.

numbers.stat: Process orchestration now has three explicit execution models (deterministic, dynamic, agentic) instead of the vague 'workflow' category.
numbers.context: This classification shift means GTM teams can now diagnose whether their automation is brittle, flexible, or actually intelligent — and pick the right one for each use case.
